newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean president apologises over son.
newsitem.headline: South Korean president apologises over son.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Saturday issued an apology over his son, who faces imminent arrest for bribery, and vowed "stern punishment" for those guilty of corruption regardless of their rank.
"President Kim again expressed regrets that the public has been given such a severe shock and disappointment through this incident," a presidential Blue House statement said.
Earlier, a Seoul court issued an arrest warrant for Kim Hyun-chul on charges of bribery and tax evasion.
"This reflects President Kim's firm intention that there should be no sanctuary when it comes to punishing corruption," the statement said.

"From now on, President Kim will sternly punish, according to the law and regardless of status or social rank, those linked to corruption," it said. "It is hoped that through this incident the corruption deeply rooted in our politics, economy and society will be expunged."

Soon after a bribes-for-loans scandal linked to the collapse of Hanbo Steel Co erupted in January, President Kim appeared on television in February and said he was ashamed his son had been linked to the scandal.
